before: Traditional PHP warnings are reported through the error system and can allow continuation. catch handles thrown Throwable objects, not every warning merely because its message describes an error.

The temporary handler converts only E_USER_WARNING to ErrorException and returns false for other severities so normal handling continues. trigger_error creates a synthetic warning. restore_error_handler in finally prevents this example from changing later policy.

ErrorException receives message, numeric code, severity, source filename and source line in that order. The code argument is 0 here; the other values come from the handler callback. Construction returns the throwable object, and throw transfers control to catch.
Expected output or behavior: converted warning. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
Optional local transfer task: Explain why blanket conversion and suppression can hide distinctions. You may trace it without a PHP interpreter; reading completion is not proof of a local run.
